findings.desc: CHK-002 userSees pins a literal tamper message that is itself the stale-enumeration defect this story removes, and the implementer correctly REFUSED to ship it. The pinned text names the signed fields as "(agentResults/issues/background/title/description/checklist were modified)" - a hand-written enumeration that goes wrong the next time the domain changes. What shipped instead renders the domain from its single declaration (INIT_CHECK_SIGNATURE_DOMAIN), which is what plan.md DoneWhen and the dispatch both asked for. AUTHOR OF THE DEFECT: the main agent, when writing the acceptance field in PLAN. The implementer flagged the conflict and reported it rather than silently self-correcting or silently complying, which is the correct behaviour. userSees is frozen from DEV (checklist_update refuses it by design, so the executor cannot move the acceptance goalposts) - this finding is the sanctioned channel for recording that the pinned criterion was superseded. RESOLUTION SOUGHT: accept the rendered message as satisfying CHK-002 acceptance, on the record, rather than reopening PLAN to edit the field. The shipped behaviour is strictly better than the pinned text.

concept-cleanup: docs/requirements/decisions/proof-or-stop-agent-prompt-consolidation-execution-plan.md:839 still asserts the PRE-CHK-002 init-check.json signature domain as current fact — "`_hash` covers story background/title/description/checklist hash/reviewRound; high/critical issues block" — implying issues/agentResults are outside the signature, which B-8df9 CHK-002 falsified (INIT_CHECK_SIGNATURE_DOMAIN now covers agentResults+issues via computeInitCheckVerdictHash). This same file explicitly states its Artifact Schema table "records current code-backed contracts", so this is not historical narrative, it is a live factual claim now wrong. CHK-005/CHK-006 fixed the equivalent stale assertions in CLAUDE.md:538/544/580 and docs/requirements/decisions/story-lifecycle.md:73, but this decision doc (also inside the story scope contracts allowedModify wildcard docs/requirements/decisions/*.md) was left unfixed — a residual reference to the redefined concept.

concept-cleanup: computeInitCheckVerdictHash (packages/main/src/core/init-check-gate.ts:169-178) defines a NEW private module-scoped canonicalJson(value) — recursive key-sorted, undefined-dropping JSON canonicalization — duplicating logic that already exists as the exported canonicalJson in packages/main/src/core/digest.ts:36-38, whose own header comment says it was extracted into a leaf module specifically "so it can be reused without dragging handler dependencies along" (already reused by core/review-run.ts). init-check-gate.ts already imports nothing else from digest.ts, so nothing blocks reuse; the two implementations sort keys by different comparators (digest.ts: a.localeCompare(b); init-check-gate.ts: a<b?-1:a>b?1:0) and diverge on null-vs-array handling, so this is not a byte-identical duplicate — it is a second, subtly different canonicalization routine for a signature/hashing code path, which is exactly the kind of unintentional near-duplicate that should not survive introducing a new signed-hash helper.
